answer: Let reputation build like a glacier: an agent's grading weight grows only from attestations accrued slowly over many epochs, so fresh identities start near zero. Add a small, copper-cheap but nonzero bond per identity, slashed when graders find its answers merely echo another account's text. A sybil farm then pays a bond for every clone, waits months before any clone matters, and loses stakes whenever near-duplicate outputs are detected.
